name: Borne Upon a Wind
oracle_text:
You may cast spells this turn as though they had flash.
Draw a card.
blocked_sentences: You may cast spells this turn as though they had flash.

needs.what: an effect op that writes a turn-scoped, per-player timing permission -- "you may cast spells this turn as though they had flash" -- that `legality._timing_ok` consults alongside the printed keyword. It must cover every spell cast for the rest of the turn, including cards not yet in hand when it resolved, and ideally carry an optional selector so narrower printings ("cast creature spells", "cast this spell as though it had flash") reach the same permission
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Casting speed is decided entirely by `legality._timing_ok` (src/commanderblitz/engine/legality.py:680), which returns True only for `card.is_instant` or `Keyword.FLASH.value in card.keywords` -- printed characteristics read off the CardDef -- and otherwise defers to the sorcery-speed window from `_can_act_at_sorcery_speed`. Nothing writable from an effect widens it. `grant_keyword` with `flash` is the tempting substitute and is wrong twice: `_timing_ok` never reads an object's granted keywords, and even if it did, an `objects` pool resolved at resolution would reach only the cards already in hand, while this line covers the whole turn -- including the card this very spell draws, which is the point of the pairing. `grant_playable` (ops_cards.py:132) is a *zone* permission (`playable_by`/`playable_turn`), letting a card be cast from somewhere other than hand at its printed timing; it moves no timing restriction. `set_turn_flag` writes a flag only `has_turn_flag` conditions read, and no legality path consults the turn ledger for casting speed. `static_effects` has `cast_from_graveyard` and `cast_from_library_top` -- again zone permissions, not timing ones. The second sentence, "Draw a card.", is plain `draw`, so only the first line is blocked and no partial answer was written. Identical to the block already recorded for Emergence Zone.
